failures.detail: On the leg that does not pin the interpreter, uv built the tool environment on Python 3.14.7, which the wheel's own metadata (Requires-Python: <3.14,>=3.12) excludes. The install reports success and every command runs, and then the health check says: Python 3.14.7 is outside the supported range >=3.12,<3.14. Exit code 4.
failures.why_not: Decision 0034: the published install command pins the interpreter, read from the bootstrap document's own requirements block. This leg exists to record what an unpinned install does on this machine — it is the observation the decision was made from, not a defect in the wheel.

installs.argv_difference: --find-links points the same requested coordinate at the candidate wheel in dist/ instead of an index, because nothing is published. The requested coordinate itself is unchanged. --reinstall is the release-engineering rule of decision 0034: this version number is rebuilt repeatedly here, and --force can serve a stale cached wheel of the same version (techtree-python-kml).

commands.isolation_note: uv, docker and hermes warn here, and docker_daemon and hermes_plugin skip behind them, only because this leg's PATH deliberately excludes the operator's tools; they say nothing about the wheel. installs.result_detail: Every command answers and every release coordinate is correct, but `techtree doctor` reports a failing health check on this interpreter: Python 3.14.7 is outside the supported range >=3.12,<3.14. That is the observation decision 0034 was made from, reproduced here against the frozen wheel. It does not stop the release, because the published install command now pins the interpreter and the pinned leg above is green.

observations.detail: The wheel declares Requires-Python <3.14,>=3.12. Left to choose for itself in a throwaway home, uv 0.12.5 (Homebrew 2026-08-14 aarch64-apple-darwin) built the tool environment on 3.14.7, which the package says it does not support. The install exits zero and all five release and catalog commands still answer correctly on it — but `techtree doctor` fails, so a first-time participant's first output would be a failed health check. The published command pins the interpreter for exactly this reason (decision 0034), and the pinned leg is green. Same finding as WP11b and WP11e, reproduced here on the frozen build.

Which interpreter the unpinned command lands on depends on the home directory it runs under, so the leg above is a property of a genuinely fresh machine rather than of this one. Under the throwaway home the legs use, uv sees only the interpreters on PATH and picks Homebrew's 3.14.7. Run again with the operator's real home — where uv already manages a CPython 3.12 — the same unpinned command instead builds the environment on Python 3.12.12 and the health check passes. Both were observed here. The throwaway-home result is the one recorded, because it is the one a new participant gets.

One earlier attempt at the unpinned leg, run with the operator's full interactive shell environment inherited instead of the explicit minimal environment recorded above, did not install at all: uv exited 1 with "Because techtree==0.1.0 requires Python >=3.12, <3.14 and you require techtree==0.1.0, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable", and created no tool environment. It did not recur under the recorded method, which was run twice, and the environment variable responsible was not identified. Recorded because it happened, not because it is understood.

Both legs install with --reinstall, never --force. Decision 0034 and ticket techtree-python-kml: --force can exit zero, print "Installed 1 package" and leave a stale cached wheel of the same version in place. Both legs then compared every payload member of the installed package against the candidate wheel byte for byte, and both legs' `release info` reported the stamped source commit 5d793b699ce75779269a67a7c2f0d9cc9c6b79de, so the bytes under these results are the bytes that were meant.

published_install_argv.detail: The install command the staged bootstrap candidate publishes, read from techtree-ash priv/releases/climb-v0.1.0/bootstrap.json. It pins the interpreter to the Python that document's own minimums block declares (3.12), which is what decision 0034 requires. The pinned leg below runs exactly this command, with --reinstall and --find-links added for release engineering. There is no published package: techtree==0.1.0 exists on no index, and nothing in this record was fetched from one. What these legs establish is that the candidate wheel's own bytes install and run on those interpreters; that the published argv is the right argv is checked separately, by tools/verify_release_core.py, whose bootstrap_cli_install_argv check passes against this document.

verdict: PASS — the published install command, interpreter pinned, is green from a throwaway home. One recorded, expected failure on the unpinned leg: the health check on an unsupported interpreter, which is why the published command pins.
